clue.text: Unlikeable character I confused with another

indicators.note: something confused has been jumbled up, so the letters lose their original order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admits they have been mixed up with another person they dislike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a letter, but here it is a figure in a story; I plus ANOTHER rearranges to ANTIHERO.
explanation.definitionFit: An antihero is a central figure in fiction lacking conventional heroic virtues, often a flawed or disagreeable protagonist.

clue.text: With no difficulty, left scoundrel

parts.note: W is a standard abbreviation for with
doing something with no difficulty is doing it with ease
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a rogue without any trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no difficulty' reads as one adverbial phrase but splits into W plus EASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel is informal for a sneaky, untrustworthy person, a figurative use from the animal's sly reputation.

clue.text: Policy going round bend, oddly? Just the opposite — it gets blanket coverage

indicators.note: done oddly means done in a strange way, so these letters come out in an unusual order
to go round something is to surround it, so one piece encircles another
this reverses the roles just described, so the outer and inner pieces swap places

parts.note: the four letters of bend, jumbled
a party line is a policy

explanation.surface: A strange policy statement about circling a bend, ending in a remark about blanket media coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the policy would go round the bend; 'Just the opposite' flips the roles so the jumbled bend surrounds the policy. 'Oddly' is not taking odd letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheets and pillowcases lie under the blankets on a bed, so they are literally covered by blankets: a witty cryptic definition.

clue.text: Is doing something artistic with others? He is

parts.note: etc. (et cetera) means and others
the contraction he's, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person is making art in a group, and the reply is yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He is' looks like the answer to the question, but it is the contraction HE'S tacked onto ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: Etching is an artistic printmaking technique, cutting a design into a plate with acid, so one who etches is making art.

clue.text: Fiddle around person who works on vessels etc.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to make small aimless adjustments

definitions.text: person who works on vessels etc.
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a travelling mender of pots, kettles and pans

explanation.walkthrough: This puzzle has double entries: each across clue serves two answers, and this one also gives 25 Across. 'Vessels' suggests ships but means pots.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinkering is idle fiddling with something, and a tinker was traditionally an itinerant mender of metal pots and pans.

clue.text: Supporter of right to include male in speculation

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a Tory backs the political right
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: A right-wing backer wants men included in some financial speculation.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party; HE goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a supposition or conjecture not yet proven, which is what a speculation is.

clue.text: In queer street, person asking others to provide answers

definitions.text: person asking others to provide answers

indicators.note: queer here means odd or peculiar, so the letters are set out strangely

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone in financial trouble goes round asking others for answers.
explanation.walkthrough: Queer Street is old British slang for debt or difficulty, fitting the bookkeeping theme. The same clue gives 24 Across, a second rearrangement of the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tester sets an exam or quiz and requires candidates to supply responses to the questions.

clue.text: Stranger's large glass

definitions.meaning: first meaning: comparative of rum, odd
second meaning: a big drinking glass

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranger' looks like a noun, an unknown person, but it is the comparative adjective; rum is British slang for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum means peculiar in British usage, so rummer is more peculiar; a rummer is also a large stemmed drinking goblet.

explanation.surface: Instructions for feeding figures into an accounting system, noting they may be entered directly.
explanation.walkthrough: The same clue serves 23 Across. In double-entry bookkeeping debits go in the left column and credits in the right, and here this answer is placed on the left side of the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Debits are entries recorded on the left side of a ledger account, and a direct debit is a familiar automatic bank payment.

clue.text: Show follower of Washington, historically, in US

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Rodgers and Hammerstein stage musical

definitions.text: follower of Washington, historically, in US
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a state that joined the Union after Washington state did

explanation.walkthrough: The same clue serves 22 Across. 'Washington' points to the first president, but here it is the state, admitted in 1889; this one followed in 1907.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma! is a famous Broadway musical, and Oklahoma is a US state admitted to the Union later than Washington.

clue.text: Seabird downloadable from Internet

indicators.note: a download pulls data out of a larger source, so the letters are extracted from within the word

parts.note: the middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: A picture of a seabird that can be downloaded online.
explanation.walkthrough: The same clue serves 21 Across, which takes a different run of letters from the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is a sea eagle, the white-tailed eagle, a large bird of coasts long used in crosswords.

clue.text: More that one artistic representation brings in equivalent to heads

parts.note: like means similar or equivalent to
a ness is a headland, so heads are nesses

explanation.surface: Several artworks bring in a sum equal to some heads, as if sold at so much each.
explanation.walkthrough: The same clue (with a misprint, 'that' for 'than') serves 18 Across with a different split. 'Heads' means headlands, not tops of bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: A likeness is a portrait or picture depicting someone, so the plural is several such pictorial depictions.

clue.text: Business practice exploiting redundancy, with first part repeated thrice in second

parts.note: surface reading: a firm making use of job cuts; really an accounting system where every transaction is recorded twice, deliberately redundant

parts.words: with first part repeated thrice in second
parts.note: setter's reading: the second word has three pairs of doubled letters, so the idea of the first word occurs three times in the second

explanation.surface: A company profits from laying off staff.
explanation.walkthrough: Redundancy means layoffs in British English, but here it is duplication: each transaction is recorded as both a debit and a credit. BOOKKEEPING has OO, KK and EE, three doubles, and the puzzle's paired clues echo the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Double-entry bookkeeping is the standard accounting method in which every transaction is entered twice, in two opposing accounts.

clue.text: Support the new? Not now

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to back the latest thing and is told to wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not now' sounds like a reply to the question, but it is the definition: a time in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Back then refers to some earlier time in the past, so it describes a period other than the present.

clue.text: Again negotiates withdrawals

parts.note: the prefix re- means again
to treat with someone is to negotiate with them

explanation.surface: Someone renegotiates the terms of their pullout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdrawals' suggests bank cash, a nod to the bookkeeping theme, but means pulling back. To treat with an opponent is an old phrase for negotiating.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is an act of pulling back or moving away, especially by an army, so retreats are withdrawals.

clue.text: Keep pressure on firm failing to terminate nincompoop

indicators.note: something that fails to terminate never reaches its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: firm means hard
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Someone leans on a company that won't fire its idiot employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terminate' suggests firing staff, but it means losing the end of the word for firm.
explanation.definitionFit: To harass is to pester or attack someone persistently, subjecting them to continual pressure.

clue.text: Bit of basic education in a bank that's more culturally affected

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a tier is a row or bank, as of seats
the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, are basic education; R is one of them

explanation.surface: A lesson in a bank that is more pretentious than its neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money, but here it is a tier, a row of things one above another. The three Rs is a stock phrase for basic schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty describes someone showily or pretentiously interested in the arts, and artier is the comparative form.

clue.text: More than one artistic representation brings in equivalent to heads

parts.note: to land a catch or a deal is to bring it in
a cape is a headland, so heads are capes

explanation.surface: Several artworks bring in a sum equal to some heads, as if sold at so much each.
explanation.walkthrough: The same clue serves 12 Across with a different split; here 'equivalent to' is the link. 'Heads' means headlands, not tops of bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Landscapes are paintings depicting scenery, so the plural is several pictures of countryside views.

clue.text: Neat an' tidy after alteration

indicators.note: after being altered, something is changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Something made neat and tidy once it has been altered, like a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat an' tidy' reads as one phrase, but only 'Neat' is the definition; the rest is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Dainty means delicately small and pretty, fastidiously neat in appearance.

clue.text: Part from religious group right about nothing

parts.note: a sect is a religious group

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone splits from a religious group over a trifling matter of rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part from' looks like a verb meaning leave, but 'Part' is a noun definition and 'from' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A sector is a distinct division or area of something, such as a section of an economy, so it is a part.

clue.text: Seabird downloadable from Internet

indicators.note: a download pulls data out of a larger source, so the letters are extracted from within the word

parts.note: letters three to six of the word

explanation.walkthrough: The same clue serves 11 Across, which takes a different run of letters from the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Terns are slender, fork-tailed birds of coasts and oceans related to gulls, so they are seabirds.

clue.text: Show follower of Washington, historically, in US

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Lin-Manuel Miranda stage musical

definitions.text: follower of Washington, historically, in US
definitions.meaning: second meaning: George Washington's aide and later his Treasury Secretary

explanation.walkthrough: The same clue serves 10 Across. Alexander Hamilton served George Washington as aide-de-camp in the Revolutionary War and as the first Treasury Secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamilton is a hit Broadway musical about Alexander Hamilton, who was a loyal lieutenant of America's first president.

clue.text: Fiddle around person who works on vessels etc.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to occupy oneself in an idle, unhurried way

definitions.text: person who works on vessels etc.
